clue.text: It may lead to penalties and, unusually, prison sentence

blocks.note: extra as an adverb means unusually, as in extra large
to do time is to serve a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A footballer's foul ends in a penalty and, unexpectedly, a spell in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, a drawn knockout match goes to an added period of play and then, if still level, to a penalty shoot-out.
explanation.definitionFit: The added period played after a draw in a knockout football match comes before any penalty shoot-out.

clue.text: Little creature, awfully rare moth, circling woman's head

indicators.note: awfully means in a terrible way, so these letters come out badly mixed up
circling means going all the way round, so the rearranged letters surround one more
the head of a word is its front, so just the first letter is kept

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
the first letter of woman

explanation.surface: A tiny scarce moth is fluttering round a lady's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the woman's actual head; it only asks for her first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthworm is a small invertebrate animal living in soil, a little creature.

clue.text: Challengers maybe defeat favourites finally

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word, so only its last letter is kept

blocks.note: to tank is slang for to thrash or defeat heavily
the last letter of favourites

explanation.surface: Underdog challengers end up beating the favourites.
explanation.walkthrough: Challenger is a British Army battle tank, so the definition is by example, flagged by 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Challengers are British Army main battle tanks, so they are examples of armoured fighting vehicles.

clue.text: Get rid of horrible boils in a hospital

indicators.note: horrible suggests something disfigured, so these letters are put out of shape

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters to rearrange
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Getting rid of some nasty boils during a stay in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish is to do away with something entirely, especially a law or practice.

clue.text: Probably doctor is ready to bandage adult

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered into a new order
a bandage wraps round something, so the rearranged letters enclose one more

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A doctor is probably ready to dress a grown-up patient's wound.
explanation.walkthrough: The A goes inside the rearranged letters, just after the D, and the result splits as a three-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: I dare say is a conversational phrase meaning I suppose, it is likely, so it can stand in for probably.

clue.text: Pass Europeans going round circuit, close to pits

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the pair of letters enclose the others
the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: two Europeans, E and E
a lap is one circuit of a track
the final letter of pits

explanation.surface: Continental drivers go round the track and pass, nearly into the pits.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural Europeans gives two Es, which sit either side: E(LAP S)E.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes or goes by.

clue.text: Heraldic insignia that is withdrawn by military forces

indicators.note: something withdrawn is taken out, so the short phrase is pulled out of the longer word

blocks.note: armies are military forces
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A coat of arms is taken away by the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A family's arms are its coat of arms, the heraldic shield and devices it bears.

clue.text: Is quieter working a necessity?

indicators.note: working means in motion, so these letters are moved round into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Must a quieter workplace be essential?
explanation.definitionFit: A requisite is something required, an essential item or necessity.

clue.text: Worn-out digital recording, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says we judge by what the ear hears

blocks.note: a CD, compact disc, is a digital recording

explanation.surface: A tired-sounding old digital recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means shabby and run-down, the state of something worn-out.

clue.text: Order soap?

blocks.note: first meaning: a sequence or succession
second meaning: a television serial, of which a soap opera is an example

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like ordering washing supplies; the question mark marks soap as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a set of things in sequence and also a run of TV episodes, which a soap opera is.

clue.text: Likelihood Norwegian's back penning musical work

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the clue words hold the answer inside them
back tells us to read the enclosed letters from right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: The chance that a Norwegian is composing a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is': the two words, back, are penning the answer, which sits backwards across likelihOOD NORwegian.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a piece of music, or movement, whose main theme keeps returning between contrasting episodes.

clue.text: Ballet posture using square beam, not quite moving

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the last letter of the word is dropped
letters that are moving shift out of their places into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
beam minus its final letter

explanation.surface: A dancer holds a pose on a square balance beam, but not quite steadily.
explanation.definitionFit: An arabesque is a classical ballet position balanced on one leg with the other extended straight behind.

clue.text: Sailor wearing hard hat is unfriendly

indicators.note: someone wearing clothes is inside them, so the sailor sits within the other letters

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
OS, ordinary seaman, is a crossword sailor
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A sailor in a hard hat is not being friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard hat' looks like one item of safety gear; it splits into H for hard and a separate word for hat, round which the sailor fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile and unfriendly are synonyms, both describing antagonistic behaviour towards someone.

clue.text: Island restricts parking in a showy manner

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the island's name closes round the other letter

blocks.note: the Mediterranean island
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean island cracks down on where cars may be left.
explanation.definitionFit: Spicily can mean in a racy, lively or flamboyant way, so it fits behaviour that is showy.

clue.text: On high moorland briefly become too warm

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: over means above, on high
heath (moorland) without its last letter

explanation.surface: Walking on the high moors, you can easily get too hot.
explanation.definitionFit: To overheat is to get hotter than is safe or comfortable, said of engines and people.

clue.text: Formerly employed by taxi firm, worker that's enthusiastic

blocks.note: ex means former
the ride-hailing company
the worker ant is crossword shorthand

explanation.surface: A cheerful worker who used to drive for a cab company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employed by' only joins the pieces, which run in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant means full of lively energy and high spirits, close to enthusiastic.

clue.text: Spare pence added to float

blocks.note: to skim is to glide or float over a surface
p is the abbreviation for pence

explanation.surface: Some loose change is put into the till's float.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Float' looks like the cash kept in a till; it is the verb. 'Added to' puts P after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to be stingy or economise, which is one verb sense of to spare.

clue.text: Assistant lawyer and friend drinking a lager abroad

indicators.note: abroad means away from its usual place, so these letters are scattered into a new order
drinking takes something inside, so the friend's letters hold the others

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A junior lawyer and a mate having a beer overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A paralegal is trained in legal work and assists solicitors or attorneys without being fully qualified.

clue.text: Unmarried male composer attends function in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the word for function is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: J.S. Bach, the German composer
a role is a function

explanation.surface: A single male composer goes to a social function after retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a party; it is a role, which is reversed after BACH.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is a man who has never married.

clue.text: Opening speaker

blocks.note: first meaning: an opening, like that of a river or cave
second meaning: a person who talks, a spokesperson or mouthpiece

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a debate's first speech; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth is an entrance such as a cave's, and also slang for someone who talks, as in loudmouth or a gang's mouthpiece.

clue.text: Repeatedly discovered that area enthralling artist in capital

indicators.note: discovered means stripped of covers, applied twice, so two words each lose their outside letters
enthralling means holding captive, so the artist is held inside

blocks.note: that with its outer letters removed
RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword artist
area with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: A painter in a capital city keeps finding the same district fascinating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' looks like found; it means uncovered, and 'repeatedly' makes it work on both following words.
explanation.definitionFit: Harare is the capital city of Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Wrecker of boat sure to be condemned

indicators.note: something condemned is wrecked or broken up, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The person who sank the vessel is certain to face a guilty verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately damages or destroys property, so is a wrecker.

clue.text: Best soldiers under the sun?

blocks.note: to best someone is to outdo them
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: The finest troops serve out in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective; it is the verb to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outdoor happens in the open air, literally beneath the sun, which the question mark flags as playful.

clue.text: Crashed out of games upset after false lie's regularly stated

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is spoken out and kept
upset means turned upside down, which in a down clue reads the word bottom to top
after places the first piece behind the second in the answer

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
PE, physical education, is school games

explanation.surface: A player knocked out of a tournament is upset after an untruthful claim is made about him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crashed out' looks like losing a match; it is slang for fallen asleep. The alternate letters A S L E come first, then PE upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To crash out is informal for falling fast asleep from exhaustion.

clue.text: I blunder when following southern mountain ranges

indicators.note: following places what comes before it after the next item in the clue

blocks.note: S abbreviates southern
taken as written
to err is to blunder
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone admits slipping up when walking behind a southerner.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged chain of mountains, a word borrowed from Spanish meaning saw.

clue.text: American over on Hawaii eating small rice dish

indicators.note: over in a down clue means flipped, so the abbreviation reads from bottom to top
eating takes something inside, so the letters hold the small one

blocks.note: US means American
S abbreviates small
HI is the postal abbreviation for Hawaii

explanation.surface: An American in Hawaii eats a small portion of rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in a down clue means placed above; Hawaii's postal code is HI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish or other toppings.

clue.text: Loathsome bowler's capacity perhaps to trap Essex's opener

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside, so one letter is enclosed
an opener comes first, so only the initial letter of the county name is kept

blocks.note: a bowler is a hat, and what it holds is a hatful
the first letter of Essex

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler is hateful for trapping the Essex opening batsman leg before wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' and 'opener' point to cricket, and Essex is an English county side; but the bowler is a hard round hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hateful and loathsome both describe something that arouses strong dislike or disgust.

clue.text: Wiping top of lamp, rather delicate

indicators.note: wiping means removing, so a letter is cleared out of the word
the top of a down word is its first letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: the top letter of lamp
fairly means rather, somewhat

explanation.surface: Dusting the lampshade is a rather fiddly job.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy as an adjective means dainty, light and fine like a fairy, hence delicate.

clue.text: One could take a flight from here?

definitions.text: One could take a flight from here?

blocks.clueFragment: One could take a flight from here?
blocks.note: surface reading: an airport, where you board a plane
setter's reading: a flight of steps, climbed from the shaft in a building that holds them

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: the flight is a set of stairs, not a journey by air.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the vertical shaft in a building containing a staircase, where you climb a flight of steps.

clue.text: Unpaid broadcasting son rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: broadcasting originally meant scattering seed, sowing
S abbreviates son

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's son is turned down for a post without pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasting' suggests radio, but its older sense is scattering seed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that is owing is still outstanding, so not yet paid.

clue.text: Small amount of time in US state wife spent

indicators.note: spent means used up and gone, so that letter leaves and another takes its place

blocks.note: T abbreviates time
the Midwestern state
W abbreviates wife

explanation.surface: A short stay in Iowa where a wife used up her money.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes in where W was spent: IOWA becomes IOTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota, the smallest Greek letter, is used to mean a tiny quantity, as in not an iota.

clue.text: Performance of substandard track on the radio

indicators.note: what comes over the radio is heard, not seen, so we go by sound

blocks.note: poor means substandard and a trail is a track

explanation.surface: A singer's performance of a weak song is played over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' suggests a recorded song; it is a path, a trail.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's portrayal of a character is their performance in the role.
